The short version

A characterful Canadian all-rye with layered bread, spice and floral character. Matched accounts support sipping and cocktails without an age statement or high-proof bonus.

Exact identity: Lot No. 40 modern recurring 100% Pot Still Rye, NAS, 43% ABV / 86 proof, 750 mL; current unmalted-rye formulation, distinct from the 1998 Guild predecessor.

Background and history

The brand first appeared in the 1998 Canadian Whisky Guild and was relaunched in 2012. Modern recurring all-rye production is scoped separately from the original reused-cask recipe.

The current producer photograph verifies the modern core, rather than a Cask Strength or Dark Oak sibling. Earlier 2012 malt-including stock is not asserted identical to every later bottle.

For the shared historical context, read Canadian whisky, cross-border trade and the American market. The release chronology above distinguishes the current bottle from its brand’s earlier history.

Producer, grains, aging and finishing

Current producer confirms all rye, copper-pot distillation and virgin white-oak maturation. Bylok’s blender-visit account describes a column pass followed by pot distillation, and a 2013 switch to unmalted rye with commercial enzymes. Pot Still in the name does not mean there was no first column distillation. Six-to-eight-year stock estimates are not a label age; a specific rye cultivar is not inferred for every current batch.

Critical review synthesis

Bourbon Culture · Bourbon Culture

The 86-proof bottle develops several sweet, herbal and floral layers with a pleasing finish. A small burned-match aroma qualifies an otherwise favorable account.

Scope: January 2020 core bottle; rumored age and American cross-category ranking are not adopted.

Kara Newman · Wine Enthusiast

Newman finds a full-bodied caramel/oak profile, developed baking spice and a persistent, oily ending.

Scope: November 1, 2015, 43% / 750 mL recurring range; current-batch continuity is not independently certified.

Published sample evidence, not first-person tasting or a representative survey. Reviewer disagreement and recipe-era limitations remain explicit; publisher grades are not mechanically converted.

Quality and calibration

Quality 7.3 / 10. Very good provisional Canadian all-rye execution. Substantive matched accounts support layered development, sweetness/spice balance and persistence; occasional sulfur-like aromatic description and batch-era limits temper exceptional claims. No American straight-rye endpoints are used.

No defensible complete Canadian native 1/5/10 framework is established for this comparison group. Seven universal execution dimensions are assessed within Canadian Single Grain / 100% Rye; unrelated American bourbon and straight-rye endpoints are not imported.

Serving recommendations

Neat

Try a small full-strength pour first and assess balance, texture and development against the attributed accounts.

Water / rocks

Add drops gradually, comparing aroma and body; cask-strength releases can change markedly with dilution.

Old Fashioned

Keep syrup restrained. For historical bottles, compare cost with the recurring core before choosing a mixing pour.

Manhattan / highball

Use a small trial serve with vermouth or soda, adjusting dilution so the rye character remains clear.

Serving suggestions are editorial starting points, grounded in documented strength and style; adjust to your taste.
